clue.text: Bill leaves Goodwood, perhaps, for a resort

indicators.note: the bill departs from the course, so its letters are removed from that word

parts.note: Goodwood is an English racecourse in Sussex, given here as an example
AC is short for account, a bill

explanation.surface: Someone abandons the races at Goodwood to head off on holiday at a resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' tells you to take AC out of RACECOURSE; Goodwood is a horse-racing course in southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A recourse is something you turn to for help, just as a resort is a last option or expedient.

clue.text: Make uneven confectionery when short of time

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so the letter is removed

parts.note: a truffle is a chocolate sweet

explanation.surface: Someone spoils a smooth chocolate when they have run out of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when short of' tells you to take T out of TRUFFLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To ruffle is to disturb a smooth surface, as wind does to hair or water.

clue.text: Pick some sweets? I'll say!

indicators.note: an exclamation about speaking, so the word is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: chews are chewy sweets

explanation.surface: A child picks some sweets and is very keen to do so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'll say!' signals a word that sounds like CHEWS.
explanation.definitionFit: To pick is to select, to make a choice between options.

clue.text: Sneaky style of bowling?

definitions.meaning: in cricket and other games, delivering the ball with the hand below the shoulder

explanation.surface: A cricketer is accused of an underarm delivery that seems unsporting.
explanation.definitionFit: A deceitful act is described with this word, and it also names a delivery with the arm kept low.

clue.text: Dog needing a pass

definitions.meaning: the Great and Little St Bernard are mountain passes in the Alps

explanation.surface: A dog is needed to get through a mountain pass.
explanation.definitionFit: The mastiff-like rescue dog is named after the hospice on the Alpine pass of the same name.

clue.text: Over a pass

parts.note: in football to cross is to pass the ball ... the field

explanation.surface: A footballer's pass goes over the defence.
explanation.definitionFit: Over and across both describe going from one side to the other.

clue.text: That man enters church to ring bell

indicators.note: enters means goes inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
him refers to that man

explanation.surface: A man goes into a church to ring its bell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enters' is the container signal: the pronoun goes into the abbreviation for the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: To chime is to sound a bell or set of bells.

clue.text: Our diet's regulated by layman

indicators.note: regulated means put in order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A non-expert controls what we eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regulated' signals rearranging OUR DIETS, keeping the S.
explanation.definitionFit: An outsider is someone not belonging to a profession or group, a non-specialist.

clue.text: Irradiated food till cooked

indicators.note: cooked suggests the words are worked over and rearranged, as figures are cooked

explanation.surface: Food left in the oven until it is cooked looks as though it has been irradiated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' signals rearranging the letters of FOOD TILL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something floodlit is lit up, bathed in beams of light, which is one sense of irradiated.

clue.text: Arm Shakespearean soldier

definitions.meaning: A braggart soldier in Henry IV Part 2, Henry V and The Merry Wives of Windsor

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean soldier takes up arms.
explanation.definitionFit: A handgun is a weapon, an arm, and Pistol is Falstaff's swaggering companion in several of Shakespeare's plays.

clue.text: Cocky divers holding in a lot of ardour

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the other pieces go inside

parts.note: divers is an old word meaning various
taken as written

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: glow is warmth of feeling, ardour

explanation.surface: Some arrogant divers are full of passion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divers' is the old adjective meaning several, not people who dive. 'a lot of' drops the final letter of the ardour word, and 'holding' wraps the result, with IN, inside the divers word.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone cocky is conceited and boastful, swollen with pride.

clue.text: Unsuccessful, so he's due for every last place

definitions.text: Unsuccessful, so he's due for every last place

indicators.note: every last asks for the final letter of each word in the run before it

explanation.surface: Someone who keeps failing is bound to finish in last place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'every last' tells you to take the final letters of Unsuccessful, so, he's, due, for; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unsuccessful who finishes last in a contest is the one beaten, the failure of the field.

clue.text: Serious actor lousy at reading

indicators.note: lousy means poor or bad, so these letters are badly arranged and must be reordered

explanation.surface: A serious actor is poor at reading his lines aloud at an audition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lousy' signals rearranging AT READING.
explanation.definitionFit: A tragedian is a performer who specialises in tragic, solemn roles rather than comedy.

clue.text: Tunnellers hope to follow Dickens' recipe for happiness

definitions.meaning: two teams digging from opposite sides want their two shafts to join in the middle
Mr Micawber in David Copperfield says happiness comes from spending less than one's income

explanation.surface: Tunnel diggers wish they could follow Dickens's advice on how to be happy.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to live within one's income, and taken literally describes two tunnel faces joining up.

clue.text: In flames — I suspect a match .

indicators.note: suspect means dubious, so the letters are unreliable and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A fire breaks out and arson is suspected in a big game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspect' signals rearranging IN FLAMES I.
explanation.definitionFit: A semifinal is a game in a knockout competition deciding who reaches the final.

clue.text: Commentator arrived in international organisation 'at a run.

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: NATO is the North Atlantic Treaty Organization
ARR is short for arrived on timetables
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A commentator turns up at an international body in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal; the run letter then follows at the end. 'at a' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrator is someone who tells or comments on a story or event.

clue.text: Tree chap planted before several others

parts.note: a chap is a man
a grove is a group of several other trees

explanation.surface: A man plants one tree before several others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'several others' means several more trees, a grove, picking up the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A mangrove is a tropical tree growing in coastal swamps.

clue.text: Magic source of light amid Lapland's obscurity

indicators.note: obscurity suggests the letters are muddled and confused, so they must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A magical light shines out from the darkness of the Lapland winter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'obscurity' signals rearranging AMID LAPLANDS, keeping the S of the possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Arabian Nights tale, the hero's lamp summons a genie, so it is an enchanted light source.

clue.text: Road traversed in car — and on foot

parts.note: ST is short for street, a road
to have ridden in a car is to have rode

explanation.surface: Someone crossed the road by car and on foot.
explanation.definitionFit: Strode means walked with long steps, moving on foot.

clue.text: Port very little in reserve

parts.note: a whit is a tiny amount
by means aside or in reserve, as in put by

explanation.surface: A port has very little held in reserve.
explanation.walkthrough: WHITBY is a fishing port in North Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Whitby is a harbour town on the Yorkshire coast of England.

clue.text: Meaning conveyed by less common retired doctor

indicators.note: something conveyed by another is carried inside it, so one piece sits within the other
retired means drawn back, so this word is read backwards

parts.note: less common means rarer
the gist of something is its meaning

explanation.surface: A doctor who has stopped work speaks in a rather unusual way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' turns the less common word into RERAR, and 'conveyed by' carries the meaning inside it. In British hospitals a registrar is a senior grade of doctor below consultant.
explanation.definitionFit: In British hospitals a registrar is a doctor ranking above a junior and below a consultant.

clue.text: Old-fashioned second' eleven say

parts.note: S is short for second
an eleven is a team, as in cricket or football

explanation.surface: A club's old-fashioned second eleven is turning out again.
explanation.walkthrough: Steam radio or steam technology is British slang for outmoded methods.
explanation.definitionFit: As in steam radio, the word describes outdated technology superseded by newer things.

clue.text: Be sold for double

definitions.meaning: to ... a price is to sell for that amount at auction
a wraith, the ghostly likeness of a living person

explanation.surface: An item goes under the hammer for twice the expected price.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods bring in a certain sum when sold, and in folklore a spectral likeness of a person is also called by the same word.

clue.text: Tool put right inside drier

indicators.note: inside places one piece within the other

parts.note: a towel dries you, so it is a drier

explanation.surface: A tool has been put right inside the clothes dryer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' puts R into TOWEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A trowel is a small hand implement used by gardeners and bricklayers.

clue.text: Provide more details about reverse covered up by old party

indicators.note: something covered up by another sits inside it

parts.note: a rout is an old word for a large fashionable evening party
to undo something is to reverse it

explanation.surface: Someone at an old-fashioned party hushes up a setback and fills in the details.
explanation.walkthrough: Rout is an archaic word for a large evening gathering; 'covered up by' puts the reverse word within it.
explanation.definitionFit: To flesh out a story or plan is to complete it with extra detail.

clue.text: City's boundaries confining ambassador

indicators.note: confining means enclosing, so one piece holds the other within

parts.note: rims are edges or boundaries
HE stands for His Excellency, the title of an ambassador

explanation.surface: A city's borders hem in a visiting ambassador.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confining' is the container signal; His Excellency is the formal style of an ambassador.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheims is a cathedral town in the Champagne region of north-east France.

clue.text: Book of songs to be accompanied by unknown old instrument

parts.note: a psalter is a book of psalms, sacred songs
Y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: A hymnbook goes with a mysterious antique instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: In algebra x, y and z are unknowns, so 'unknown' gives Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A psaltery is an ancient stringed instrument plucked with fingers or a plectrum.
